newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rail mergers to continue, reasons will change.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rail mergers to continue, reasons will change.

text.p: U.S. railroad mergers will continue, but they will be driven less by savings than by the need to provide high level service, according to Norfolk Southern Corp chief executive David R. Goode.

He also told the Traffic Club of Chicago Thursday "railroads are doing a credible job" on safety and efficiency, but the industy has "a long way to go in improving service quality and flexibility." A text of Goode's remarks was made available in New York Friday.
U.S. railroads "have gone from the 'big seven' to the 'big five' in just one 12 month period," he pointed out.
"Mergers are likely to continue because they are a key tool in our quest to satisfy our customers' demands for flexible, quality transportation," Goode said.
"The shape of future mergers will be driven less by consolidation savings than by the synergies necessary to provide high level service," he added.

Noting the parcel business "can track and monitor your precious shipment from one end of the trip to the other," Goode said that level of information "is the benchmark against which the rest of us in the transporation business are measured."
Railroads, he pointed out, "are the only transportation mode that still 'intelines traffic'."
He said Norfolk Southern has built relationships to blur the traditional lines between railroads.
This allows its intermodal trains to reach Miami on Florida East Coast Industries Inc tracks.

Norfolk Southern sold half of its Triple Crown Services retail intermodal company to Conrail Inc "because we knew we had to reach out beyond the limits of Norfolk Southern owned trackage," Goode said.
He said Norfolk Southern and Conrail also redesigned their joint auto shipping network and instituted Northeast-Southeast double stack service.

With Conrail and Union Pacific Corp Norfolk Southern organized a jointly owned container pool and it serves the Des Moines, Iowa, grant markets through a "symbiotic relationship with Burlington Northern Santa Fe" Corp.
While he is "proud of these initiatives," they have "limitations. They take a long time to negotiate and they tend to be fragile." -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
